newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong had wettest year in over a century.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong had wettest year in over a century.

text.p: The first eight months of this year has been Hong Kong's wettest period in 113 years, since records began here in 1884, weather experts said on Friday.
During the period, 2,611.3 mm of rain was recorded, breaking the previous record of 2,610.4 mm set in 1973.
A Hong Kong Observatory official attributed the unusually wet period to effects of the El Nino phenomenom.
"I believe it's related to a phenomomen called El Nino, which means temperatures over equatorial waters in the east Pacific are very much above normal," director C.Y. Lam said.
"It disrupts global circulation. One of the effects is to create a lot of moist and warm air coming into Hong Kong."

Rainstorms which lashed the territory in July caused further floods and landslips this week as the wet summer showed no let-up. The latest floodwaters inundated over 1,000 homes, swamped farmland and wrecked fish ponds.
